segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הֶיתֵּר נְדָרִים — פּוֹרְחִין בָּאֲוִיר וְאֵין לָהֶם עַל מָה שֶׁיִּסָּמֵכוּ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» Incidental to the Festival peace-offering, the mishna describes the nature of various areas of Torah study. The halakhot of the «dissolution of vows,» when one requests from a Sage to dissolve them, «fly in the air and have nothing to support them,» as these halakhot are not mentioned explicitly in the Torah. There is only a slight allusion to the dissolution of vows in the Torah, which is taught by the Sages as part of the oral tradition.

segments.he: הִלְכוֹת שַׁבָּת, חֲגִיגוֹת וְהַמְּעִילוֹת — הֲרֵי הֵם כַּהֲרָרִים הַתְּלוּיִן בִּשְׂעָרָהּ, שֶׁהֵן מִקְרָא מוּעָט וַהֲלָכוֹת מְרוּבּוֹת. הַדִּינִין וְהָעֲבוֹדוֹת הַטְּהָרוֹת וְהַטְּמָאוֹת וַעֲרָיוֹת — יֵשׁ לָהֶן עַל מָה שֶׁיִּסָּמֵכוּ, וְהֵן הֵן גּוּפֵי תוֹרָה.
segments.en: «The halakhot of Shabbat, Festival peace»-offerings, «and misuse» of consecrated property «are like mountains suspended by a hair, as they» have «little» written about them in «the Torah, and» yet the details of their «halakhot are numerous.» The details of «monetary law,» sacrificial «rites, ritual purity and impurity, and» the halakhot of «those with whom relations are forbidden» all «have something to support them,» i.e., there is ample basis in the Torah for these halakhot, «and these are the essential parts of Torah.»

moves.summary: dissolution of vows has no support
these have support and are the essentials of Torah

positions.claim: dissolution of vows floats in the air; Shabbat, festival offering and meila are mountains hanging by a hair; civil law, sacrifices, purity and arayot are well supported
